questions.question: After `SimpleEmbedder.fit(["refund policy", "refund timing"])`, what does `embed("refund")` contain?
options: A probability distribution over the two documents, with one score per document
A fixed one-hot vector whose only nonzero entry is the word `refund`
A normalized TF-IDF vector over the fitted vocabulary
A binary vector produced by hashing the complete sentence into 64 bits
questions.explanation: `SimpleEmbedder` builds a sorted vocabulary and IDF values during `fit`. `embed` then computes term frequency times IDF and L2-normalizes the resulting vocabulary-sized vector.

questions.question: Why does `cosine_similarity` return `0.0` when either input vector has zero norm?
options: A zero vector is always maximally similar to every other vector in the index
The function treats empty vectors as a request to use Euclidean distance instead
The IDF calculation guarantees that zero vectors cannot occur after fitting
It avoids division by zero because a zero vector has no direction
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity divides by both vector norms. The implementation explicitly returns zero when either norm is zero, which gives unknown-only or empty text a safe neutral score.

questions.question: A query contains a word absent from `SimpleEmbedder`'s fitted vocabulary. What happens to that word in `embed`?
options: It is ignored, so it contributes no coordinate to the TF-IDF vector
It is appended to the vocabulary and changes the dimensions of every stored vector
It raises `KeyError`, because every query token must have appeared during fitting
It receives the highest possible IDF so that unknown terms dominate retrieval
questions.explanation: The embedder loops through tokens only when their lowercase form is in `word_to_idx`. Unknown words are skipped; the fitted vector shape remains stable for indexed documents and queries.

questions.question: What does `VectorIndex.search(query_vector, top_k=2, metric="euclidean")` sort by?
options: The largest raw Euclidean distance, because distant documents are more informative
Negative distance, sorted so nearest vectors come first
The number of shared nonzero coordinates, which is the Hamming metric
The original insertion order, because Euclidean search does not return scores
questions.explanation: The index represents Euclidean similarity as the negative distance. Sorting scores descending therefore puts the smallest actual distance at the top, while preserving a common result shape.

questions.question: Why does `truncate_embedding(vector, 3)` renormalize the sliced vector?
options: Slicing creates new vocabulary terms that must be assigned IDF values
Renormalization converts the vector to a binary Hamming representation
Slicing changes the norm, so it is renormalized for cosine use
The function cannot return fewer dimensions unless every coordinate sums to one
questions.explanation: A prefix slice generally has a norm below one. The helper slices first and divides by the new norm, preserving the scale expected by cosine-based retrieval unless the slice is all zeros.

questions.question: How does `chunk_by_sentences(text, max_chunk_tokens=200)` differ from fixed word chunking?
options: It always returns exactly 200 sentences, regardless of the text length
It embeds each sentence independently and returns vectors rather than text chunks
It overlaps every sentence with the previous chunk by 50 tokens, even when the sentence is complete
It groups complete sentences under the token budget
questions.explanation: The sentence-aware helper splits on sentence boundaries and accumulates sentences while their estimated token count stays within the limit. Fixed word chunking can cut a sentence in the middle.
